Bill.BriefDescription: Managing the health of the state's forest.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to managing the health of the state's forests;amending RCW 76.06.020, 76.06.040, 76.06.030, 76.06.050, 76.06.060, and76.06.070; adding new sections to chapter 76.06 RCW; and creating a newsection.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that the paramountduty of the state is to provide for the education and wellbeing of itschildren. Washington has been blessed with an ample forest land basethat, because of the wisdom of its founders, is held in trust by thestate to provide a sustainable economic mechanism for educationfunding. However, the great forests of the state cannot provide forthe next generation on its own. To maximize the potential benefit tothe educational system, the forests of the state must be activelymanaged and maintained, using modern silvicultural techniques and soundforest stewardship. When land managers fail at this mission, or havetheir efforts hamstrung by third party litigation roadblocks, the groupthat bears the cost is the state's children. Therefore, thelegislature further finds that the state should make deeper investmentsin the health of its forests, provide local mechanisms to aid the state p. 1 HB 2642in its management duties, and require third parties that influenceforest health management to reimburse the state's children for thecosts inflicted upon the children.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 76.06.020 and 2003 c 314 s 2 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The definitions in this section apply throughout this chapterunless the context clearly requires otherwise. (1) "Agent" means the recognized legal representative,representatives, agent, or agents for any owner. (2) "Department" means the department of natural resources. (3) "Owner" means and includes persons or their agents. (4) "Timber land" means any land on which there is a sufficientnumber of trees, standing or down, to constitute, in the judgment ofeither the department or a county executive authority when appropriate,a forest insect or forest disease breeding ground of a nature toconstitute a menace, injurious and dangerous to permanent forest growthin the district under consideration. (5) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of public lands. (6) "Exotic" means not native to forest lands in Washington state. (7) "Forest land" means any land on which there are sufficientnumbers and distribution of trees and associated species to, in thejudgment of the department, contribute to the spread of forest insector forest disease outbreaks that could be injurious to forest health. (8) "Forest health" means the condition of a forest being sound inecological function, sustainable, resilient, and resistant to insects,diseases, fire, and other disturbance, and having the capacity to meetlandowner objectives. (9) "Forest health emergency" means the introduction of, or anoutbreak of, an exotic forest insect or disease that poses an imminentdanger of damage to the environment by threatening the survivability ofnative tree species. (10) "Forest insect or disease" means a living stage of an insect,other invertebrate animal, or diseasecausing organism or agent thatcan directly or indirectly injure or cause disease or damage in trees,or parts of trees, or in processed or manufactured wood, or otherproducts of trees. HB 2642 p. 2 (11) "Integrated pest management" means a strategy that usesvarious combinations of pest control methods, including biological,cultural, and chemical methods, in a compatible manner to achievesatisfactory control and ensure favorable economic and environmentalconsequences. (12) "Native" means having populated Washington's forested landsprior to European settlement. (13) "Outbreak" means a rapidly expanding population of insects ordiseases with potential to spread. (14) "Person" means any individual, partnership, private, public,or municipal corporation, county, federal, state, or local governmentalagency, tribes, or association of individuals of whatever nature.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 76.06.040 and 1951 c 233 s 4 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Every owner of timber lands, including timber lands owned by thestate and managed by the department, or ((his)) the owner's agent,shall make every reasonable effort to control, destroy, and eradicatesuch forest insect pests and forest tree diseases which threaten theexistence of any stand of timber or provide for the same to be done ontimber lands owned by him or her or under his or her control. In theevent ((he)) the owner fails, neglects, or is unable to accomplish suchcontrol, the action may be performed as provided for in this chapter.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 76.06.030 and 1988 c 128 s 16 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Except as otherwise provided, this chapter shall be administered bythe department.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 76.06.050 and 1988 c 128 s 17 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1)(a) Whenever the department finds timber lands, that are managedby a person or entity other than the department, threatened byinfestations of forest insects or forest tree diseases, and if it findsthat such infestation is of such character as to threaten destructionof timber stands, the department shall declare and certify aninfestation control district and fix and declare the boundaries p. 3 HB 2642((thereof)) of the control district, so as to definitely describe suchdistrict. ((Said)) The district may include timber lands threatened bythe infestation as well as those timber lands already infested. ((Thereafter)) (b) The department shall at once serve writtennotice to all owners of timber lands or their agents within the((said)) district to proceed under the provisions of this chapterwithout delay to control, destroy, and eradicate the ((said)) forestinsect pests or forest tree diseases as provided herein. The ((said))notice may be made by personal service, or by mail addressed to thelast known place or address of ((such)) the owner or agent. ((Said))The notice shall list and describe the method or methods of action thatwill be acceptable to the department if the owner or agent elects tocontrol, destroy, and eradicate ((said)) the insects or diseases on hisor her own property. ((Said)) (c) The notice when published for five consecutive days inat least one daily newspaper or in two consecutive issues of a weeklynewspaper, either paper having a general circulation in ((said)) thedistrict will serve as the written notice to owners of noncommercialtimber lands. (2)(a) When the threatened timber lands occur on property managedby the department, the authority to declare an infestation controldistrict transfers to the lead executive authority of the county inwhich the land is located. If the infestation control area is locatedin more than one county, then the lead executive authority of allinvolved counties must act in concert. (b) Once an infestation control district has been identified by acounty executive authority, notice must be immediately provided to thecommissioner along with a directive to proceed under the provisions ofthis chapter without delay to control, destroy, and eradicate theforest insect pests or forest tree diseases identified by the county.Control efforts may include the removal of dead trees, standing or not,that can serve as incubators for future forest health issues.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 76.06.060 and 1988 c 128 s 18 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) If the owner or agent ((so)) notified ((shall fail, refuse,neglect)) by the department under RCW 76.06.050 fails, refuses, orneglects or is unable to comply with the requirements of ((said)) the HB 2642 p. 4 notice, within a period of thirty days after the date ((thereof)) ofthe notice, it shall be the duty of the department or its agents, usingsuch funds as have been, or hereafter may be, made available to proceedwith the control, eradication, and destruction of such forest pests orforest tree diseases with or without the cooperation of the ownerinvolved in a manner approved by the department. (2) In instances where a county executive authority notified thedepartment of the creation of an infestation control district ondepartmentmanaged land, it is the duty of the department to complywith the requirements of the notice within thirty days of receipt. Ifthe department fails, refuses, or neglects to comply with therequirements of the notice, the county executive authority may proceedwith the control, eradication, and destruction of forest pests orforest tree diseases with or without the cooperation of the department.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 76.06.070 and 1988 c 128 s 19 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Upon the completion of the work directed, authorized, andperformed under the provisions of ((this chapter)) RCW 76.06.060 by thedepartment on lands not managed by the department, the department shallprepare a verified statement of the expenses necessarily incurred inperforming the work of controlling, eradicating, and destroying((said)) forest insects or forest tree diseases. The balance of suchexpenses after deducting such amounts as may be contributed to thecontrol costs by the state, by the federal government, or by any otheragencies, companies, corporations, or individuals, shall be a lien tobe prorated per acre upon the property, or properties involved((:PROVIDED, That)). However, the amount of ((said)) the lien shall notexceed twentyfive percent of the total costs incurred on such owner'slands including necessary buffer strips. ((Said)) The lien shall bereported by the department to the county assessor of the county inwhich ((said)) the lands are situated, and shall be levied andcollected with the next taxes on such lands in the same manner and withthe same interest, penalty, and cost charges as apply to ad valoremproperty taxes in this state((: PROVIDED FURTHER, Such)). Further,the report and levy shall be made only on commercial timber lands. Theassessor shall extend the amounts on the assessment roll in a separatecolumn, and the procedure provided by law for the collection of taxes p. 5 HB 2642and delinquent taxes shall be applicable thereto, and, upon thecollection thereof, the county treasurer shall repay the same to thedepartment to be applied to the expenses incurred in carrying out theprovisions of this chapter. (2) Upon the completion of the work directed, authorized, andperformed under the provisions of RCW 76.06.060 by a county executiveauthority on lands managed by the department, the county shall preparea verified statement of the expenses necessarily incurred in performingthe work of controlling, eradicating, and destroying the forest insectsor forest tree diseases on departmentmanaged land. The departmentshall fully reimburse the county within thirty days for all costsinvolved in the recovery effort from the resource management costaccount created in RCW 79.64.020.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 76.06 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In any eradication or control effort on departmentmanaged landexecuted by either the department or a county executive authority underRCW 76.06.060, the party implementing the control effort must includeprovisions to sell all salvageable timber. The proceeds of all sales,regardless if conducted by the department or a county, must bedistributed in the same manner as other timber sales from the sameproperty.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 76.06 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Any party that brings a judicial or administrative actionleading to a final judgment that results in the inability of thedepartment or a county to fulfill the duties of this chapter or executethe authority of this chapter is required to reimburse the state forthe actual value of all revenue lost from the sale of otherwisesalvageable timber prohibited by the judicial or administrative order. (2) Lost revenues recovered under this section must be distributedin the same manner as provided for salvage timber sales in section 8 ofthis act.
